content: Otesaconazole is contraindicated in females of reproductive potential, pregnant women, and lactating women due to potential risks. Based on animal studies, there is evidence that fetal harm may occur if exposed to this drug. There is no available data on the presence of otesaconazole in human or animal breast milk, its effects on milk production, or its impact on breastfed infants. Otesaconazole has a half-life of 138 days, with 56% of the drug excreted via feces through biliary excretion and 26% excreted in urine. The drug should be administered with food, and capsules must be swallowed whole without chewing, crushing, dissolving, or opening. It should be stored at a temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F).
